title: Avoid full TensorView axis-label index materialization
finding: TensorView.__post_init__ duplicated every canonical sorted axis label into a transient nested label-to-index dictionary before validating sparse entries and sorting them. With up to 16 axes and 100000 labels per axis this construction scaled transient retained state with all declared labels even when the sparse entry set touched only a tiny subset. The module already had binary lookup over canonical sorted labels for coordinate indexing.
primary_claim: TensorView construction now reuses the canonical sorted axis label tuples directly and performs exact binary lookup with bisect_left for entry validation and ordering. It no longer creates a full auxiliary label-index mapping. Fourfold/Forest source identity, tensor status, provenance, duplicate-claim refusal, canonical ordering and public wire contracts remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the already canonical, sorted TensorAxis.labels storage and the existing stdlib bisect dependency. Do not add an index cache, builder, alternate tensor type, lookup service, planner, store or backend abstraction merely to avoid the transient duplicate map.
acceptance: TensorView validates entry labels without iterating every label merely to construct an auxiliary lookup map
entry canonical ordering remains derived from the exact canonical axis order
